clue.text: Stand-in for substitute?

blocks.note: surface reading: a replacement player or actor taking someone's place
setter's reading: the word 'stand-in' is a word meaning the same as 'substitute'

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a question about understudies, but it is really about vocabulary: one of these two words can replace the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another is exactly what the two hyphenated and plain terms are to each other.

clue.text: Most learned of gossip going round East Street

indicators.note: turning round sends a word back the way it came, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: to gas is to chatter or gossip
E is the compass abbreviation
ST is the address abbreviation

explanation.surface: Neighbours on a street compete over who is the cleverest gossip in the east end.
explanation.walkthrough: To gas is British slang for chatting idly; 'going round' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage means wise or knowledgeable, and its superlative describes the wisest person.

clue.text: Northern Liberal appearing in feature about who looks down on Londoners?

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word runs backwards
something appearing inside another thing sits within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
the nose is a facial feature
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician from the north features in a piece about a snob who looks down on Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSE reversed is ESON; L goes inside it to make ELSON, after N. Nelson's statue stands on top of Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Nelson's statue stands high on its column in central London, literally gazing down at the crowds below.

clue.text: Man scratching head hard during screen work, missing sleep?

indicators.note: to scratch out the head is to strike off the opening letter
something happening during another thing falls within it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a knight is a man, a piece in chess
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
to screen material is to sift it

explanation.surface: A man scratches his head at a computer screen, doing work while short of sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, 'man' means any piece, which is how a chess piece can stand for a man here; the question mark flags that sleeplessness is only a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Working a shift through the night means doing your job during the hours usually given over to rest.

clue.text: French sea temperature restricting island’s value

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: mer is the French word for sea
T is the abbreviation for temperature
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: The temperature of the French sea limits how valuable an island is to tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: T holds I to give IT, which follows MER.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or quality, something deserving praise, so it matches value as a noun.

clue.text: An Idiot Abroad location

blocks.note: taken as written
a twerp is a silly or foolish person

explanation.surface: An Idiot Abroad is a British TV travel show in which comedian Karl Pilkington is sent round the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of the TV show hides the split: 'An Idiot' is the wordplay and 'Abroad location' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium, so for a British reader it is a place overseas.

clue.text: Something pointed found in – gASP! – A RAGU Sauce

indicators.note: found in says the answer is sitting inside the following run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run straight through the exclaimed words

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in shock at a pointed object discovered in a ragu sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letters show where the answer runs across the punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus spears have tapered tips, so the vegetable is fairly described as a thing with a point.

clue.text: Cheers over busker in the centre getting charge

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the letters there are kept

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks
the two central letters of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A busker performing in the town centre gets cheered, then gets charged for the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above; 'ta' is everyday British for thank you, often used as cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge can be a duty or responsibility entrusted to someone, which is a synonym of an assigned job.

clue.text: Vision of nearly 19, agreed to split up

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
splitting something opens a gap in it for another piece to sit in

blocks.note: the answer to 19 down
yes signals agreement

explanation.surface: A dream of nearly nineteen people agreeing to break up.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is not a number but a cross-reference to the answer at 19 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision in its physical sense is the faculty of seeing with one's eyes, which is the answer word exactly.

clue.text: Public address finally announces game that’s shown both sides of border?

definitions.text: that’s shown both sides of border?

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: PA is the abbreviation for a public address system
the closing letter of the word
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: A stadium announcer calls a match being broadcast in two neighbouring countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a game televised in two countries; the definition is instead a document presented at passport control when leaving and entering.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers present this travel document to officials when leaving one country and again when entering the next.

clue.text: Spooner’s toilet humour seen in prison

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of word pairs

blocks.note: loo is British slang for a toilet; it takes the other word's opening sound
a gag is a joke; it takes the other word's opening sound

explanation.surface: Crude toilet jokes are what you hear among prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO GAG becomes GOO LAG, which is said the same as the Soviet camp system's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The gulag was the Soviet network of forced-labour camps, so the word now stands for a harsh prison.

clue.text: Take back some dreSSES, SO PERfect on the counter

indicators.note: some means a portion of the words, so the letters sit inside them
counter means running against, so the letters go the opposite way

blocks.note: the capitalised run across the three words

explanation.surface: A shopper returns some dresses to the shop counter, even though they looked perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' looks like the shop counter where returns are handled, but it means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to reclaim goods, typically when payments were not kept up, so it means to take back.

clue.text: Anecdot?

blocks.note: surface reading: a misspelt word for a little tale
setter's reading: the word for a tale, cut short by one letter

explanation.walkthrough: An anecdote is a brief tale; printed without its final E, the word itself has been made shorter, so it is a tale made brief twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief narrative piece of fiction or an anecdote is a tale of small length, and this one is literally truncated.

clue.text: Struggle to shift this person’s record covers

indicators.note: a cover wraps round what it protects, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: an LP is a long-playing record
this person is the speaker, I, and 'this person is' is I'm

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper finds it hard to sell their stock of record covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' suggests selling stock, but here it means move about.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp is to walk with difficulty, moving along unevenly because of an injured leg.

clue.text: ExtRA IN FOR ESTablished part that’s steamy

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing that is steamy

indicators.note: a part is a portion of the preceding words, so the letters sit inside them

blocks.note: the capitalised run across the four words

explanation.surface: An extra is cast in an established role in a steamy drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steamy' suggests a racy scene; here it means hot and humid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical forests are hot and humid, with moisture rising as vapour from the dense canopy.

clue.text: Parking roasting pan out back, batter that man the starter of red snapper

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction
a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: P is the sign for parking
roasting weather is very hot
how things pan out is how they go
to batter or rap is to strike
he is the pronoun for that man
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A cook recalls a recipe: roasting pan out, then battering the fish, red snapper.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen words mislead: 'snapper' is not the fish but slang for someone who snaps pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper is informal slang for someone who takes pictures, especially a press cameraman.

clue.text: Deviously omitting to stick around wife?

definitions.text: Deviously omitting to stick around wife?

indicators.note: acting deviously means going by a crooked route, so the letters are rearranged
sticking around something surrounds it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband slyly fails to stay faithful to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranged letters wrap round W, and the sentence also describes a cheating spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timing means deceiving a partner by secretly seeing someone else, which is failing to stay loyal to one's spouse.

clue.text: The old woman with face to kiss, on base done with this?

definitions.text: The old woman with face to kiss, on base done with this?

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman
the opening letter
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics
something done with is finished, over

explanation.surface: A mother wants her face made kissable, with foundation, and a beauty treatment does it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as the definition: an old woman's face, with its base layer of make-up, being transformed.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeover is a cosmetic transformation of a person's appearance, often starting with foundation applied to the skin.

clue.text: Upper-class, protected by corrupt palace after maiden I’ve offended

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled and altered, so the letters are reworked
a thing protected by another is shielded inside it
after places one piece following another in the reading order

blocks.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for upper-class

explanation.surface: A maiden offends an aristocrat sheltered in a corrupt royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap round U, and M goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is an admission of fault, literally 'through my fault', said by someone confessing a wrong.

clue.text: Drunk teens conga about from moment it’s legal

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled
about can mean around, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent

explanation.surface: Tipsy teenagers dance a conga line from the moment they are allowed to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of the two words wrap round OF.
explanation.definitionFit: The age of consent is the point in life at which the law treats a person as able to agree to sex.

clue.text: Top cycling? Not even on the podium!

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so a letter moves from one end to the other

blocks.note: the height of something is its peak or top

explanation.surface: A cycle race result: the rider was nowhere near the top three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like the sport of the surface; it tells you to move the first letter of HEIGHT to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Only the first three finishers stand on the podium, and this ordinal place is far behind them, well out of the medals.

clue.text: Container goods European Commission holds up

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: EC is the abbreviation for European Commission
G is short for good, so two of them give the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: The European Commission holds up a shipment of containerised goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds up' looks like a phrasal verb for delaying, but it splits into a container instruction and a word taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cup is a small holder for a boiled egg at breakfast, so it is one kind of vessel.

clue.text: And what have you applied with husband getting cut?

blocks.note: etc, et cetera, means and so on
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone asks what you have put on, now that your husband has had his hair cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And what have you' is a phrase meaning 'and other such things', the same as et cetera.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design into a surface, cutting lines with a tool or acid.

clue.text: Four members per side engaged in combat?

definitions.text: Four members per side engaged in combat?

blocks.clueFragment: Four members per side engaged in combat?
blocks.note: surface reading: a small team of four on each side in a battle

blocks.clueFragment: Four members per side engaged in combat?
blocks.note: setter's reading: each fighter uses four limbs, two arms punching and two legs striking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' means limbs, not team members: each of the two fighters uses both fists and both feet.
explanation.definitionFit: This combat sport allows striking with feet as well as gloved fists, so all four limbs are used.

clue.text: It floats up and down

indicators.note: reading the same going up the grid as going down means the letters are symmetrical

blocks.note: a small paddled boat, whose letters are symmetrical

explanation.surface: Something bobs on the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and down' looks like the motion of a boat on the swell, but in a down entry it means the word reads the same from top or bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: This small paddled boat is a craft that sits on water, carrying one or two paddlers.

clue.text: Try to sit on one that’s for hire

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing that is for hire

blocks.note: to try or tax someone is to strain their patience
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tries out sitting in a chair that is available to rent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sit on' puts TAX above I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab carries paying passengers, and its roof light shows when it is available for a fare.

clue.text: False gravity punctured by university lecturer’s opening bawdy remark

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so the letters are in a made-up order
the opening of a word is its first letter
a puncture lets something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A don's pompous seriousness is punctured when he opens with a rude joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters take U and L after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgarity can mean a single coarse or crude expression, the kind of dirty joke implied by the definition.

clue.text: Good day to break into 21, ultimately lacking moral code

indicators.note: lacking the ultimate letter means losing the last one
breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: the answer to 21 across
both are greetings

explanation.surface: A burglar picks a nice day to break in, showing no morals at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is a cross-reference to the answer at 21 across, and 'good day' is a greeting, not a fine day.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of principles of right conduct, a system of values governing behaviour.

clue.text: Heard nude group like a nice fire?

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the answer is judged by its sound

blocks.note: raw can mean naked, and a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: Word goes round that a group of naturists like sitting by a warm fire.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent RAW RING and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaring fire is one blazing strongly and cheerfully, the image of a cosy hearth.

clue.text: King, 21, happy to get extra for English breakfast?

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the answer to 21 across
to feel up is to be in good spirits

explanation.surface: A king, aged twenty-one, is delighted to be served more at his fry-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is not an age but the answer at 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato sauce is a common condiment added to a full English breakfast of eggs, bacon and sausages.
